main_body: Tile-roofed cottage: a large sloped roof (rows 2-42) over a cream plaster and timber front wall (rows 43-78) with a stone-framed door and a shuttered window
top_band: Roof slope from row 3 to about row 41, shading from light salmon #e0a07c at the top to dark red-brown #561d26 at the eave. A dark eave line at rows 41-42 separates it from the cream wall.
evidence: The roof reads as a large tiled slope seen from above, with a dark eave line and shadow that overhang the wall. Below it is a distinct front wall with timber framing. The door has a stone surround and the window has shutters and a projecting sill, so these read as inset rather than painted flat. This matches how the Beodeul house references draw their roofs. There are no receding side faces.

style.evidence: The roof has about six tonal steps, with per-tile highlights and dark seams, which is comparable to the references. The outline is tinted (dark red-brown at the roof, dark brown at the timber) and 0% of dark edge pixels are neutral. The plaster has speckle and the door has plank grain. Flat-fill coverage is only 2%. The median of 10 colours per tile is close to the stone reference (11) but below h101 (18), and the 42 total colours are below both references (185 and 66). That makes it slightly lower in density, but not shallow or sticker-like.
